content.title: About
content.content: Peanut butter cookie is a crunchy biscuit that incorporates peanut butter into the dough. It combines the sweetness of sugar with the creamy taste of peanuts, making a popular snack suitable for both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial production of peanut butter cookies began in the United States in the 1930s.
Peanut butter used in cookies is often natural peanut paste without added sugar or salt.
Peanut butter cookies are frequently used as a base for dessert bars and ice‑cream sandwiches.
In some countries the cookie is a traditional school snack.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 25 % protein, which helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats in peanuts support heart health.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Peanuts are a good source of iron, essential for blood formation.

items.title: Supports blood‑sugar stability
items.content: The low glycemic index of peanut butter helps keep glucose levels steady.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: People with peanut allergy may experience severe reactions when consuming the cookie.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The fat content makes the cookie energy‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened versions can contribute to tooth decay and metabolic issues.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Some brands add salt and preservatives, which may be undesirable for those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peanut butter cookies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, crumbled into yogurt or ice cream, or used in dessert recipes such as cakes and cheesecakes. For children, choose varieties without added sugar or excess salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
